title: Apache Kafka
subtitle: A distributed, replicated commit log for durable event streaming.

tiles.label: Producers
tiles.says: Producers append records to topics in batches.
tiles.detail: Keys choose partitions, preserving order per key. Batching and compression raise throughput.

tiles.label: Delivery acks
tiles.detail: Idempotent producers and acknowledgements trade latency for durability explicitly.

tiles.label: Schemas
tiles.detail: Versioned formats let producers and consumers evolve independently.

tiles.label: Topics & partitions
tiles.says: Topics split into ordered, append-only partitions.
tiles.detail: Partitions scale throughput and define the ordering guarantee.

tiles.label: Replication
tiles.says: Each partition has a leader and in-sync followers.
tiles.detail: Losing a broker elects a new leader, so streams survive hardware failure.

tiles.label: KRaft quorum
tiles.says: KRaft controllers manage metadata with Raft.
tiles.detail: Removing ZooKeeper simplifies operations and speeds up recovery.

tiles.label: Consumer groups
tiles.detail: Adding consumers scales reads horizontally, and each partition has one reader per group.

tiles.label: Offsets
tiles.says: Committed offsets record each group's position.
tiles.detail: Consumers resume after failure and can replay history to rebuild state.

tiles.label: Retention
tiles.says: Retention keeps data by time, size or compaction.
tiles.detail: Replay windows support recovery and new consumers, and compaction keeps the latest value per key.

declarations: Order is guaranteed per partition, never per topic.
Consumers pull; offsets belong to the group.
The log is the source of truth.
